newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Nine killed in two separate attacks in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Nine killed in two separate attacks in Colombia.

text.p: Gunmen murdered nine people in two separate attacks in Colombia's oil-rich eastern plains and the violence-wracked city of Medellin, police said on Monday.

Masked men broke into a house in Pore, in eastern Casanare province, early on Monday, shot five people to death and kidnapped a woman and two young children, a police spokesman said. They later murdered two men on a farm outside the town.

Police in the provincial capital Yopal were still investigating the motives for the attack on Monday afternoon but said they had no clues on the identity of the attackers. The National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest guerrilla force, and right-wing paramilitary gangs are active in the cattle-rearing and oil-producing region.

The second attack occurred late on Sunday in the northwest city of Medellin, where a mechanic and a taxi driver were shot to death by unknown assasins. Local media said the two were former guerrillas who had laid down their arms to return to civilian life but police were unable to confirm this.

The attacks came in the wake of the murder of four men, two of them ex-guerrillas, on a bus in Medellin on Saturday and a massacre in a remote region of northwest Antioquia province, first reported on Saturday. Police fear the final death toll of that attack may be as high as 15 and not the eight initially reported. Paramilitary groups have been blamed for the killing.
